## Purpose

`NixlPushConnector` rejects a pipeline-parallel prefill whose stages hold Mamba/SSM groups, and rejects `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` altogether. Kimi K3.1 (MLA + SSM, DCP) can therefore not use a TP x PP prefill engine in a NIXL push P/D deployment.

## Purpose

Kimi K3 turns sequence parallelism (SP) off whenever `pipeline_parallel_size > 1`, and asserts on it at the stage boundary. A TP8 x PP2 MegaMoE prefill therefore runs every stage on the full token set.

This PR keeps SP on under PP for the MegaMoE path, the way DeepSeek-V4 does (#65766): a non-last stage all-gathers the sequence-sharded hidden state, the AttnRes residual blocks and the aux hidden states before it returns `IntermediateTensors`, and the next stage shards them again. items.author: gty111

items.body:

## Overview

A Mooncake EC consumer waits for a push for every multimodal item, even when the request has no `ec_transfer_params` and no encoder will push. A raw-media request sent straight to the consumer waits `push_wait_timeout_s` (60s) and returns 500. Like `ECCPUConnector`, the consumer now leaves such requests to the local encoder.

## Claims

- Raw-media requests to a Mooncake EC consumer are encoded locally: 200 in about 1s instead of 500 after 60s.
- Requests that carry `ec_transfer_params` (the normal EPD path) are unchanged.

## Validation

1 GPU per s

items.title: [Fix] layernorm_sp: Reserve Torch symmetric-memory workspace for the largest SP pass
items.author: vineelbhat
items.summary: On a LayerNorm SP pass, unquantized bias-free linears, such as Kimi-K3.1's dense layer 0, run Torch's and. These grow their symmetric-memory workspace on demand, and growing it frees the old one.
items.body:
## Motivation

On a LayerNorm SP pass, unquantized bias-free linears, such as Kimi-K3.1's dense layer 0, run Torch's `fused_all_gather_matmul` and `fused_matmul_reduce_scatter`. These grow their symmetric-memory workspace on demand, and growing it frees the old one. Prefill graphs are captured at up to 4,096 tokens, so the first longer eager pass, such as a 16,384-token chunk, grows the workspace, and the next graph replay uses freed memory.

## Modifications

- Before the first fused call, the workspace is reserved once for the largest SP pass: `chunked_prefill_size`, or `max_prefill_tokens`

items.body:
## Motivation

With LayerNorm SP inside breakable prefill graphs, a Kimi-K3.1 graph body returns this rank's hidden-state shard, which has 1/TP of the rows, and DFlash aux hidden states for all rows. The backend trims both to the shard's row count, so the aux hidden states come back with 1/TP of their rows and the next indexing kernel asserts out of bounds.

## Modifications

- `_output_rows` returns a row count per output, and the backend slices and copies each output to its count, so the aux hidden states keep all their rows.

items.title: [Fix] qwen4-exp: Scale BF16 PLE shards before FP8 storage
items.author: xuqianmamba
items.summary: When a checkpoint sets but stores BF16 PLE shards, the loader casts them to FP8 with scale=1. Small values lose precision or become zero.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #49493.

When a checkpoint sets `ple_embedding_dtype="float8_e4m3fn"` but stores BF16 PLE shards, the loader casts them to FP8 with scale=1. Small values lose precision or become zero.

## Modifications

Compute `amax / 448` for each checkpoint shard before TP slicing, then quantize the local rows. Regular lookup and offload prefetch apply the scale for the requested row. Zero shards get a positive minimum scale; native FP8 checkpoints keep their supplied scalar scale.

Using one scale per shard avoids holding the full BF16 table in memory or requantizing earlier shards.

- All-sliding-window GQA DSpark drafts (e.g., 5-layer GQA `sliding_window=2048` on Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark) run unsharded (`dcp_size=1`) on the draft worker. - Reusing `DFlashDraftKVRing` with a ROCm-specific Triton window index kernel shrinks the draft pool to `0.12 GB` GPU HBM and `0 GB` Host GTT (105x reduction), freeing HBM directly for the target KV pool

Under pipeline parallelism, the OffloadingConnector's scheduler sizes the CPU pool from stage 0's KV bytes per block, while each worker uses its own stage's, so they disagree on the number of CPU chunks and on each worker's CPU page size. items.title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] All-gather wo_b's MXFP8 input instead of all-reducing its output on large steps
items.author: fanxingran
items.summary: Switches DeepSeek-V4.1 `wo_b` from all-reducing bf16 output to all-gathering MXFP8 input under TP on ROCm gfx950, reducing per-rank communication and improving decode throughput.
items.body:
## Overview

With tensor parallelism on ROCm, DeepSeek-V4.1's attention output projection `wo_b` all-reduces its `[M, 5120]` bf16 output on every layer. On large steps this PR all-gathers `wo_b`'s MXFP8 input instead (2.4x fewer bytes a rank at TP2, 4.8x at TP4) and runs the whole `wo_b` on every rank, so those steps have no all-reduce after the attention.

## Claims

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X (gfx950), DSpark speculative decoding, this PR against the commit it is applied to:

- TP2, 8k-in / 1k-out, 48 / 64 concurrent requests: output throughput **+4.2% / +5.0%**, mean TTFT **-9.0% / -9.

items.author: GaGa55555LaLa
items.summary: On ROCm, the modular MoE kernel only aliases to the caller's when AITER MoE is enabled. On the default Triton path, therefore copies into after every. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the modular MoE kernel only aliases `fused_out` to the caller's `output` when AITER MoE is enabled. On the default Triton path, `TopKWeightAndReduceNoOP` therefore copies into `output` after every `moe_sum`. This PR drops that ROCm/AITER special case so the alias behaves like on CUDA.

Fixes #68173

## Claims

- Removes one D2D copy per MoE layer per forward on ROCm without AITER (the default).
- MoE outputs are bitwise identical to main.

### What does this PR do?

`preprocess_thd_engine` packs a jagged `NestedTensor` into a flat THD buffer with
one Python loop iteration per sequence. When `cp_size == 1` the nested tensor
already stores its rows in THD order, so the `input_ids[i]` inside that loop is a
round trip through `NestedTensor.__torch_dispatch__` — a C++ → Python → C++ hop,
GIL acquisition, operator-table lookup and a fresh subclass object — all to return
a slice of `values()` that is already contiguous.

## Motivation

With `--dsa-*-backend prims_ts`, `PrimsTSSparseMLA` plans a FlashInfer Prims-TS sparse MLA kernel the first time a row count needs it, and a plan compiles its CuTe DSL kernel. CUDA graph warmups cover the captured decode shapes, but eager batches (prefill chunks, decode batches above the graph sizes) compile kernels while serving. One cold compile takes tens of seconds, and every request in that batch waits for it. On a prefill server this shows up directly as tail latency.

This PR compiles those kernels when the DSA backend is built, before the server reports ready.

## Motivation

The peer reader in #49474 lets a GPU read KV pages directly from another GPU's pool in the same NVLink domain. The reader first imports the source pool's memory through a CUDA FABRIC handle, so the source pool must be backed by CUDA VMM allocations created with `CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_FABRIC`. items.author: abenezeradane
items.summary: Fixes dots/hy_v3/hy_v4 tool parsers to emit valid JSON by preserving raw text for non-finite numbers and large integers instead of converting them through float/json.loads.
items.body:
## Overview

The `dots`, `hy_v3` and `hy_v4` tool parsers convert `number` tool-call arguments with `float()` or `json.loads`. A model value of `1e400` or `nan` reaches the client as `{"amount": Infinity}` or `{"amount": NaN}`, which is not valid JSON, so a strict client's `json.loads(arguments)` fails. `dots` also turns `12345678901234567890` into `12345678901234567168`. This PR keeps integer literals exact and, like the shared `coerce_to_schema_type` helper (#43984, #55743), keeps values that JSON cannot hold as their raw text.

With `RoutedScaleMode.OUTPUT` and shared experts, `MoERunner` scales the routed expert output in place and then adds the shared expert output: two elementwise passes over `[tokens, hidden]` per MoE layer. - Bit-identical to the current path where it applies: a power-of-two scale multiplies exactly, and BF16 / FP32 adds round the sum once either way.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Fix lost worker-failure notification race in MultiprocExecutor
items.author: huangsiyuan0422
items.summary: Fixes a race condition where a failure callback registered concurrently with the monitor thread can be orphaned, silently leaving dead workers undetected.
items.body:
Fixes #69292

## Purpose

`register_failure_callback()` and the `MultiprocWorkerMonitor` thread formed an unlocked check-then-act pair over `(is_failed, failure_callback)`:

```python
# register thread
if self.is_failed:          # R1 check
    callback()
else:
    self.failure_callback = callback   # R2 store

# monitor thread
self.is_failed = True       # M1 set
...
callback = self.failure_callback      # M2 fetch
if callback is not None:
    self.failure_callback = None      # M3 clear
```

items.title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Stream plain replies that start with "[" in xlam and hunyuan_a13b
items.author: abenezeradane
items.summary: Fixes xlam and hunyuan_a13b tool-call parsers that incorrectly withheld plain-text streams beginning with '[', returning empty content instead of the actual reply.
items.body:
## Overview

With `--tool-call-parser xlam` or `hunyuan_a13b`, a streamed chat reply that starts with `[` but is plain text (for example `[1] Paris is the capital of France.`) is held back as a possible tool call and never sent, so the client gets empty content while the non-streamed reply is correct. This PR makes both streaming parsers treat a leading `[` as a tool-call array only when it can still be an array of objects, and sends the withheld text once it is not.

items.title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen4Exp] Grouped QSA indexer scorer for MTP verify rows
items.author: maeehart
items.summary: The current kernels score each row on its own, so each key tile is loaded 1 + k times. This PR adds a grouped kernel for verify batches.
items.body:
## Purpose

With MTP, every decode request sends 1 + k query rows to the QSA indexer, and they all score the same compressed keys. The current kernels score each row on its own, so each key tile is loaded 1 + k times.

This PR adds a grouped kernel for verify batches. One program takes the rows of one request, loads each key tile once, scores all rows and index heads with one `tl.dot`, then sums the heads with a second small dot. Scores differ from the tiled kernel only in the order of the fp32 sums.

It is used only when the batch has no prefill rows and every decode request has the same row

On Hopper, Muse Spark's ModelOpt NVFP4 routed experts run on Marlin W4A16. items.title: [Spec Decode] Sparse top-K draft cache for probabilistic drafting (`draft_top_k`)
items.author: Madhav-Kanda
items.summary: Adds an opt-in: probabilistic drafting proposes from, and verifies against, the drafter's top-K tokens, so the dense draft-logits cache is replaced by a K-entry sparse cache. The output distribution is unchanged, and the freed memory goes to the KV cache.
items.body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in `speculative_config.draft_top_k`: probabilistic drafting proposes from, and verifies against, the drafter's top-K tokens, so the dense `[max_num_reqs, num_speculative_tokens, vocab_size]` draft-logits cache is replaced by a K-entry sparse cache. The output distribution is unchanged, and the freed memory goes to the KV cache. Related: #67770, #56724.

## Claims

- **Memory-limited serving** (Gemma-4-26B + DFlash, TP2, 36 GiB/GPU, concurrency 128): +22% output tok/s vs dense probabilistic drafting and +10% vs greedy, from 47% more KV-cache tokens than dense.

## Motivation

items.title: [Perf] hunyuan_v4_flash: Length-aware decode top-k for the IndexPool
items.author: BBuf
items.summary: Makes decode top-k in Hy4-flash IndexPool length-aware so each row skips padding columns, reducing logits and top-k kernel time by ~0.7ms per step.
items.body:
## Motivation

Hy4-Flash decode spends a fixed amount of IndexPool work per DSA layer that grows with the configured context, not with the requests. The decode CUDA graphs size the logits for the longest context (65536 groups at the default 262144-token context), so every DSA layer wrote -inf up to that width for each row and then ran a top-k over the whole row. In a bs=16 decode profile on B300 (TP4, FP8) the logits kernel took 35.4 us and the top-k 22.4 us per DSA layer, about 0.7 ms of a 10.8 ms step.

## Modifications

- `indexpool_logits(..., lengths=...)`: the kernels write each row's sc

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Finish HF3FS saves of preempted requests before reuse
items.author: lkhun9311
items.summary: Fixes a race condition in HF3FS KV connector where preempted request saves could finish gathering after their blocks were reassigned, corrupting another request's KV cache.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #69269. `HF3FSKVConnector` now implements `handle_preemptions`. Before a step that preempts a request runs its forward or starts loads, it waits until every tracked save of that request has finished its gather into device buffers, or has ended with any gather work it already enqueued fenced. It doesn't directly wait for the 3FS write or the metadata confirm that follow a gather.

Thank you to the maintainers and to everyone who built the HF3FS connector and its in-tree mock client and metadata server, which made this testable on a single small GPU. Special thanks to @kam

- `%Q` and a trailing `%` produce a template error instead of a process panic.

items.title: [Fix] function-call: start qwen3_coder structural tag on the <tool_call> token
items.author: rlaope
items.summary: The structural tag from xgrammar triggers on the text. If the model writes any other separator after (blank line, space, CRLF, none), the trigger never matches, so the strict tool schema is never applied and the call is parsed with arguments the schema forbids…
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #45225.

The `qwen_3_coder` structural tag from xgrammar triggers on the text `<tool_call>\n<function=`. If the model writes any other separator after `<tool_call>` (blank line, space, CRLF, none), the trigger never matches, so the strict tool schema is never applied and the call is parsed with arguments the schema forbids.

xgrammar 0.2.9 adds `get_model_structural_tag(..., token_markers=True)`, which for `qwen_3_coder` dispatches on the `<tool_call>` token and then forces the canonical `\n<function=NAME>\n`. SGLang never passes it.

## Overview

Moves the per-layer context gathers of PCP + DCP prefill off the main stream for DSA models (`flashmla_sparse` with `fp8_ds_mla`, e.g., GLM-5.x, DeepSeek V3.2) via two opt-in `ParallelConfig` flags (default off), plus two always-on indexer prefill bugfixes.

- **`--pcp-dcp-kv-prefetch`** (default off): Prefetches layer l + 1's FP8 context KV over NVLink symmetric memory via copy engines while layer l attends (whole prior context for indexer layers; cross-rank selected-row union, ~7% near 1M, for top-k-reusing layers).
- **`--pcp-dcp-gather-overlap`** (default off): Exchanges each

On SM12.x (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, RTX 50 series) the diffusion runtime defaults to Torch SDPA, which runs PyTorch's FA2 kernel (`pytorch_flash::flash_fwd_kernel`). cuDNN ships an sm120 SDPA kernel (`cudnn_generated_fort_native_sdpa_sm120_flash_fprop_*`) that is faster on dense non-causal diffusion attention.

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Back off the last prompt token for sliding-window READ P/D
items.author: shiannn13
items.summary: Fixes a sliding-window bug in MoRIIO READ where the decoder reads null blocks freed by prefill; backs off by one token to realign.
items.body:
## Overview

MoRIIO READ has the sliding-window bug from #65550, on the **prefill** side. The prefiller frees out-of-window blocks for all N prompt tokens before it publishes its block table. The decoder then READs the null block into the block holding the oldest position its recomputed token (N - 1) attends to. This PR backs the READ sliding-window prefill off by one token, as #65584 does for NIXL/Mooncake. It also aligns the decoder's sliding-window blocks, because a backoff alone shifts the whole window by one block.

## Claims

- MoRIIO READ + sliding window: the decoder no longer reads

items.title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Preserve BERT segment IDs during breakable CUDA graph replay
items.author: yuyz-cyber
items.summary: Fixes incorrect BERT segment embeddings during breakable CUDA-graph replay by copying request-level token_type_ids into a shared device buffer.
items.body:
## Overview

With breakable CUDA graphs enabled, `LLM.score` can return incorrect BERT relevance scores because it ignores the boundary between the query and the document. BERT uses `token_type_ids` to distinguish query tokens from document tokens. vLLM omits these IDs from the dummy inputs used during graph capture, so the graph never records the operation that marks document tokens. On replay, BERT therefore assigns the same segment embedding to both parts of the input.

## Claims

- BERT scoring uses the current request's segment IDs during graph replay.

items.author: athrael-soju

items.body:
1.4.0rc3, C++ cache transceiver over UCX, hybrid model (48 linear-attention + 16 full-attention layers).

`kv_cache_size` only counts paged KV: 82 to 86 MiB for ~1.3k-token prompts, while each handoff moves ~166 MB because the recurrent state (78 MB per slot) goes over too. So it reads ~48% low.

`rnnCacheFormatter.cpp` never calls `updateKvCacheSize`, though `cacheFormatter.cpp` does.

items.title: [Quantization] Online FP8: use the weight-only kernel table on GPUs without FP8 GEMMs
items.author: 14H034160212
items.summary: Where the kernel is chosen from depends on how the model was quantized: - compressed-tensors FP8 ( on these GPUs) and online FP8 with pick from: Humming, then Marlin. This PR makes pick from the weight-only table on those GPUs, like the other two paths.
items.body:
## Purpose

On CUDA GPUs without FP8 GEMMs (SM75/80/86), FP8 linears always run weight-only (W8A16). Where the kernel is chosen from depends on how the model was quantized:

- compressed-tensors FP8 (`CompressedTensorsW8A16Fp8` on these GPUs) and online FP8 with `activation: null` pick from `_POSSIBLE_WFP8A16_KERNELS`: Humming, then Marlin.
- Online `fp8_per_tensor`, which is what `--quantization fp8` gives, picks from the W8A8 table and lands on Marlin.

This PR makes `Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod` pick from the weight-only table on those GPUs, like the other two paths. GPUs with FP8 GEMMs

items.title: [Security] Bound Rust video memory per request
items.author: jperezdealgaba
items.summary: The Rust frontend decoded every video in a request concurrently and retained the decoded clips and preprocessed tensors without an aggregate memory limit. A request with multiple clips could exhaust server memory despite per-item limits.
items.body:
## Summary

The Rust frontend decoded every video in a request concurrently and retained the decoded clips and preprocessed tensors without an aggregate memory limit. A request with multiple clips could exhaust server memory despite per-item limits. Bound video memory across the request, fetch and decode clips sequentially, and reject requests that exceed the limit with a client error.

## Changes

- Account for compressed video bytes and decoded frames before retaining each clip, then account for preprocessed video tensors before building engine features.
- Reject over-budget MuseSpark video

items.author: 14H034160212
items.summary: On an A100, a 4096 -> 64 projection takes 37 us with FP8 weights and 45 us with int4 g128 weights. A BF16 cuBLAS GEMM of the same shape takes 6 us, and a 4096 -> 4096 Marlin GEMM takes 12 to 14 us. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Purpose

Dense Marlin GEMMs with very few output tiles are slow, and they get slower as N shrinks. On an A100, a 4096 -> 64 projection takes 37 us with FP8 weights and 45 us with int4 g128 weights. A BF16 cuBLAS GEMM of the same shape takes 6 us, and a 4096 -> 4096 Marlin GEMM takes 12 to 14 us.

`marlin_mm` always launches `sms * blocks_per_sm` blocks. With one or two output tiles, the kernel's striping gives each block about one K tile, so each output tile's K is split across ~100 blocks. Those blocks then reduce through the workspace locks one after another, and the length of that chain

items.author: Ar4ikov
items.summary: Under spec decoding, computes logits and runs the sampler for one row per dummy request. A verify step computes them for every draft position, rows. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

Under spec decoding, `profile_run` computes logits and runs the sampler for one row per dummy request. A verify step computes them for every draft position, `num_reqs * decode_query_len` rows. `warmup_kernels` runs such a step only after the KV cache is sized, so with a large vocabulary it OOMs there. ## Overview

With MoRIIO in WRITE mode, any request with `n > 1` (parallel sampling, e.g. RL rollouts) hangs forever and leaks KV on both prefill and decode. All `n` children carry the router's single `transfer_id`, and WRITE mode keys its pairing by `transfer_id` alone. This gives each child its own transfer id, `f"{transfer_id}#{i}"`, derived identically on both sides in `on_new_request`.

items.title: [Perf][Kernel] Mamba2 SSD chunk_scan: launch all heads of a chunk together
items.author: chanakyagt
items.summary: chunkscanfwdkernel puts chunks on grid axis 1 and heads on grid axis 2, so the GPU runs every chunk of head 0, then every chunk of head 1, and so on. Each chunk's 256 x 256 fp32 CB block (from bmmchunkfwd) is read by every head of its group.
items.body:
Fixes #69206

## Overview

_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel puts chunks on grid axis 1 and heads on grid axis 2, so the GPU runs
every chunk of head 0, then every chunk of head 1, and so on. Each chunk's 256 x 256 fp32 CB
block (from _bmm_chunk_fwd) is read by every head of its group. While the CB blocks of all chunks
in one call fit in L2 this costs nothing; once they do not (on an RTX 4060 Ti with 32 MB of L2,
past about 16k tokens per call), every head re-reads them from DRAM and the kernel's time per
token jumps.

This PR swaps the two grid axes, so all heads of a chunk run together and share its CB

```
items.title: [V1 FSDP] update_weights broadcasts full params every step (~9s/step on 32B); no delta or bucketed sync mode
items.author: dahai80
items.summary: On the V1 FSDP path, (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the full parameter set every training step. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed.
items.body:
## Summary

On the V1 FSDP path, `update_weights` (actor → rollout engine weight sync) broadcasts the **full parameter set every training step**. Measured cost on Qwen2.5-32B TP8: ~9 s/step, every step, regardless of how few parameters changed. Over hundreds of GRPO steps this is a fixed tax proportional to model size, not to actual weight drift.

## Suggestion

A bucketed delta mode would remove most of this cost:

- hash/checksum per parameter bucket, sync only buckets whose checksum changed (in practice almost none change every step in RL fine-tuning — the update is small relative to init)

`LogitsProcessor._apply_head` has a fast path for `head_dtype=float32` that

bf16/fp16 inputs is implemented on XPU (torch 2.15.0+xpu, the version pinned in
```

items.title: [Perf][Model] Inkling 2: back only readable sconv-state blocks on SM12x
items.author: abtraore
items.summary: Reduces per-request short-conv state KV memory from ~3 GB to ~54 MB on SM12x by backing only the blocks later steps can read, using DFlash-style null leading blocks.
items.body:
## Overview

Inkling 2 stores its 48 short-conv states (W=4) as tiny-window sliding-window KV groups, and each request reserves `W - 1 + max_in_flight_tokens` positions of bf16 conv state per group even though a later step only reads the 3 positions before its first token. On SM12x with TP=1 this PR backs only the blocks a later step or a prefix hit can read (DFlash-style null leading blocks) and skips conv-state stores into the null block. Addresses #54703 for Inkling 2 on SM12x.

## Claims

- RTX 5090 (32 GB), `thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini`, FP8 KV, one GPU: the per-request conv-state r

items.author: mawong-amd
items.summary: Two changes, one idea: the rows of the tile table only pay off when takes them; when the shape routes to the fragmented tile, which loses to at for every dtype — so those shapes now fall back to on wave64. And on gfx950, bf16 uses the packed dot instead of the…
items.body:
## Overview

Two changes, one idea: the `YTILE 3/4` rows of the `wvSplitK` tile table only pay off when `sml_` takes them (`M % tile == 0`); when `M % tile != 0` the shape routes to the fragmented `hf_` tile, which loses to `sml_` at `YTILE 2` for every dtype — so those shapes now fall back to `YTILE 2` on wave64. And on gfx950, bf16 uses the packed `v_dot2_f32_bf16` dot instead of the MFMA path whose `floatx4` accumulators spill at `YTILE 3/4`, so the N=5 bf16 `YTILE=2` pin drops there. gfx942/gfx90a keep MFMA and the pin; their device code is unchanged.

`__HIP__MI3XX__` stays the family

items.author: xrennvidia
items.summary: With N > 1, each LM head (main and MTP) projects, scores and differentiates the sequence one N-th at a time, so the fp32 logits are never allocated for the whole sequence. Results match the unchunked head up to rounding and no work is repeated.
items.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Adds `lm_head_loss_num_chunks` (`--lm-head-loss-num-chunks`, default 1 = off). With N > 1, each LM head (main and MTP) projects, scores and differentiates the sequence one N-th at a time, so the `[seq, batch, vocab]` fp32 logits are never allocated for the whole sequence. Results match the unchunked head up to rounding and no work is repeated.

**Why:** with a large vocabulary the logits set peak memory. For 8192 tokens and a 262k vocabulary, one head holds 8 GiB of logits plus a 4 GiB copy

items.title: Activation checkpointing runs during torch.no_grad()
items.author: sbhavani
items.summary: Fixes activation checkpointing incorrectly entering CheckpointFunction under torch.no_grad, causing stale recompute state during forward-only RL log-probability computation.
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

`tensor_parallel.checkpoint()` enters `CheckpointFunction` under `torch.no_grad()`. The wrapped forward sees `is_checkpointing() == True` and can queue state for a backward recompute that never runs. 

Miles hit this during forward-only RL log-probability computation. [code](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f0987cfeb8d358637cddd054e270f757a0dd53cf/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py#L796)

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**

With a CUDA tensor `x`, run `checkpoint(fn, False, x)` inside `torch.no_grad()`. Have `fn` print `is_checkpointing()`. It prints `True`.

## What

The NVLS AllGather-V and ReduceScatter-V kernels, and the ordered ReduceScatter-V used by batch-invariant mode, returned before their barrier when a CTA's `pid >= ep_max_tokens`. So whether a CTA took part in the cross-rank barrier depended on a device value (`ep_max_tokens`) that nothing checks is equal on every EP rank.

With this change every CTA enters the barrier. CTAs without rows only skip the copy loop, which is already bounded by `local_tokens`.

## Why

This is a robustness change, not a fix for an observed bug.

items.summary: In V1 trainers ( and ), whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas splits the batch into optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted ad…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8766.

In V1 trainers (`sync` and `colocate_async`), `_compute_advantage()` whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()` splits the batch into `ppo_mini_batch_size` optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than `ppo_mini_batch_size`, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted advantage means, introducing chunk-level policy-gradient drift.

This PR re-normalizes `mini_batch_td["advantages"]` per optimizer chunk in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`

items.title: [Bug] TransferQueue drops samples after a 30 s ACK timeout, then compute_log_prob fails with KeyError: 'loss_mask' (Qwen2-7B GSM8K GRPO recipe)
items.author: AmineDiro
items.summary: On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the baseline in ) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log and carry on.
items.body:
## Summary

On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the `qwen2-7b-fsdp2.log` baseline in `docs/algo/baseline.md`) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log `Timeout waiting for data status update ACK from controller after 30s` and carry on. The data was written to storage but the controller never marks it ready, so the trainer later gets an empty batch from TransferQueue and fails with `KeyError: 'loss_mask'` in `compute_log_prob`.

The timeout itself is a slow controller.

### Bug Description

## Description

This PR adds DeCo-Attention to VisualGen as an opt-in quantized-attention recipe of the `CUTEDSL` backend. The QK product of self-attention runs on NVFP4 operands, with the quantization error of the scores compensated inside the same matrix product; the PV product runs in FP8, or in NVFP4 on SM120. On Wan2.2 T2V at 720p the denoising is 1.68x faster than with BF16 attention on GB300, 1.73x on Rubin and 1.69x to 1.85x on RTX PRO 6000.

```yaml
attention_config:
```

```
items.author: yijingl-nvidia
items.summary: This PR lets git worktrees of TensorRT-LLM share one ccache. A fresh worktree then reuses the objects that another worktree already compiled, so its first build is much faster.
items.body:
## Description

This PR lets git worktrees of TensorRT-LLM share one ccache. A fresh worktree then reuses the objects that another worktree already compiled, so its first build is much faster.

Before this PR, a fresh worktree missed ccache for every compile. ccache keys each object on its compile command, and that command holds the absolute paths of the source and build folders. A worktree at a new path therefore gets new keys. ccache's `base_dir` setting fixes this, but each user has to configure it. CI configures it in `jenkins/controlCCache.groovy`.
```

Under model parallelism a rank reads a whole sample out of TransferQueue and then throws most of it away. This PR lets each rank fetch only the part it will actually use, by running a small `data_parser` on the storage unit so the discarded bytes never cross the network.

Hydra 1.4 rejects parent traversal (`../group`) in Defaults Lists:

items.title: [algo, trainer, fsdp, megatron, cfg, doc] feat: add topk_rb KL loss (top-k Rao-Blackwellised KL to the reference)
items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

# RFC: Independent Restart of Faulty Rollout Replicas — Detection, Isolation, and In-Place Rebuild, Training Never Stalls

> **Status**: Ready for Review |
> **Related**: FT RFC **#8380** (this RFC is its rollout-side sub-item, tracking the 26Q4 roadmap **#8186** item "Rollout replica restart without interrupting trainer"); demo draft PR **opened** (in-fork review copy, 7 commits): **https://github.com/HaoWang113/verl/pull/2** |
> **Prior art**: #8168 (standalone replica lifecycle APIs prototype PR — mechanism-level borrowing)

---

When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, `rollout/raw_reward` gives that episode extra weight. ### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

items.body:
## Problem and behavior

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device. Ordinary Ray groups retain their behavior, and duplicate ownership/topology checks remain. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

items.author: R0k1e
items.summary: upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with, so the whole logits tensor is copied to fp32.
items.body:
## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. The LM head GEMM has already rounded these values to bf16, so the copy adds memory but no precision. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

The fp32 copy does one useful thing: every consumer of the logits computes in fp32 because its input is fp32. This PR keeps that guarantee, but enforces it

The `math` reward path accepts distinct large integer answers as equal. For example, a prediction of `9007199254740993` receives a correct reward when the reference is `9007199254740992`.

items.author: LingYi-Liang
items.summary: This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close. With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 wh…
items.body:
## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

With valid finite log-probabilities near -0.1, I reproduced a value of -1.4901161e-8 where an 80-digit reference gives 4.9986626e-11. The helper feeds the reported KL term and configured KL loss/reward paths; the Search-R1 example selects `low_var_kl` with a nonzero KL-loss coefficient.

## Problem

With `--partial-rollout`, a sample aborted mid-generation goes back to the data buffer and is resumed later. `generate()` resumes it with a `max_new_tokens` budget reduced by `sample.response_length` and appends the new tokens after the existing response, so the request must be conditioned on that response.

For samples with images, the request is built as:

```python

payload["text"] = sample.prompt
```

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.author: Domin-Focus
items.summary: Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct response scores 0 under. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.
items.body:
## Problem

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

```python
if not ground_truth:
    return False
ground_truth = str(ground_truth)
```

Labels are passed through from the dataset as-is (`slime/utils/data.py:272`), so a zero answer arrives as `0` or `0.0`. Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct `\boxed{0}` response scores 0 under `rm_type=math`. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Those paths expect, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.
items.body:
## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.
- Preserve the original nested return shape for d

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.body:
Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

items.summary: For example: was parsed as: This corrupts padded or otherwise -containing environment values. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged.
items.body:
## Summary

- Preserve `=` characters after the first separator in the space-separated `extra_env_vars` fallback parser.
- Add regression coverage to the always-on CPU test matrix.

## Problem

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

`TOKEN=abc== END=ok`

was parsed as:

`{"TOKEN": "abc", "END": "ok"}`

This corrupts padded or otherwise `=`-containing environment values.

## Change

Use `split("=", 1)` so only the key/value separator is consumed. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.
